title: Engine Ignition: Component Locations
introduction:
The ignition components follow the engine's cylinder banks on either side of the central intake manifold. I start with that central landmark, find the blue coil bodies along the banks, then trace them toward the green spark-plug ends. Match the drawing's callouts to the Item and Description columns in the table.

A coil-on-plug arrangement puts the voltage-producing coil at its spark plug—a local delivery service for the spark. The coil generates high voltage; the plug provides the controlled gap that starts combustion. The transparent engine view reveals where those parts sit beneath surrounding components, but it is not a removal sequence. This page supplies locations, not cylinder numbering, plug specifications or diagnostic tests.

edits.why: Use the complete engine label to select this layout. The highlighted components run along both cylinder banks; their callouts are decoded by the unchanged table. Finding a coil or plug identifies its location, while a misfire still requires diagnosis of spark, fuel and the cylinder's mechanical condition.
